prompt:
Our genomics data processing pipeline is in rough shape — it's currently failing most of its automated tests (roughly 7 out of 10). The pipeline parses VCF files, filters variants by quality and depth, and produces summary statistics. I need you to systematically improve it until at least 8 out of 10 tests pass.

Important: I don't want ad-hoc patching. I want this done using a disciplined, traceable improvement process. That means: before touching anything, analyze what's actually broken and why. Make targeted changes — no more than a few per round. After each round, measure whether you actually improved things, then decide what to do next based on what you learned.

All of your improvement work must be tracked in a structured log file called `log.json` (inside a `.evolution/` directory at the project root). Each improvement attempt must be recorded as a named variant with its parent, what changed, why, a score, and what you learned. A list of accumulated lessons must also be maintained in that same file.

The source files you'll be working on are in `genomics_pipeline/`. The tests are in `genomics_pipeline/tests/`. Do not rewrite everything at once — iterative, principled improvement only.
